stage: MA24 G03 correction and tool-receipt learning lease expiry
implementation: Both initial claim reads use clock_timestamp instead of transaction-start now for the five-minute lease window.
Message correction requires the current owner/run/token/processing state and unexpired wall clock in the final ready UPDATE RETURNING; zero rows throws extraction_lease_expired.
Receipt learning requires the same fresh lease before renewing updated_at; an expired lease cannot be revived. Zero rows throws and rolls back receipt-derived observations.
Existing extraction orchestration requeues extraction_lease_expired under its original lease token, without contacting the model or overwriting a different lease.

checks.unitTests: 73 passed across four files, including correction final-update rejection, receipt renewal rejection, and orchestrator retry for both failures
checks.expirySequence: For each function, seed a processing job aged 299 seconds, then delay its actual observation INSERT by 2.2 seconds via an owner-scoped AFTER INSERT trigger. Final wall-clock lease rejection rolls back the entire function transaction; observation/notice/outbox counts remain unchanged and job status/token/updated_at remain exactly original.
checks.positiveControl: The same 2.2s delay with a fresh lease commits one observation/notice/outbox. Correction reaches ready and clears token; receipt learning stays processing with its original token and renewed time.
checks.cleanup: Scoped trigger/functions and synthetic accounts, runs/messages, receipts, extraction jobs, observations/notices/conflicts/outbox removed from the isolated clone.

limits: Expiry verifier calls the two actual transaction functions directly. Database rollback and orchestrator requeue are proven separately by database and unit checks, not as a complete running Worker flow.
A near-expiry seeded timestamp plus real delay crosses the natural clock boundary; the verifier does not wait a full five minutes or inject scheduler death/new-owner takeover during this interval.

Earlier receipt learning, correction and ordinary extraction remain separate transactions; this is not whole-job atomicity or a new complete source-row protection claim for correction/receipt learning.
